title: Offers and pricing
hired_for: To make every price, discount, bundle, threshold and guarantee earn more gross profit per order, and to stop discounts from quietly training buyers to wait.

jobs.job: Show me what each discount really costs in gross profit before it runs
jobs.why: A 20% off code can wipe out half the profit on an order. If the owner only sees revenue, a busy sale can lose money.

watch.metric: gross profit per order after discount, per offer, against the owner's floor
watch.source: Shopify orders, discount codes and cost per item

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a 25% off sale looks like a record week at $80,000, but profit per order falls from $18 to $6. After: the model runs first, the sale goes out at 15% off a bundle and profit per order holds at $14.
jobs.who_today: founder or finance lead, after the sale

jobs.job: Set the free shipping line where it pays for itself
jobs.why: Set too low, free shipping eats margin. Set too high, it puts buyers off. The line should sit just above where most orders land today.

watch.metric: share of orders just over the free shipping line, and shipping cost per order, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: free shipping at $25 when the average order is $38, so 90% of orders ship free. After: the line moves to $45 and average order value rises to $44.

jobs.job: Make the offer beat the buyer's biggest doubt, with a price that still makes money
jobs.why: Most offers are just a discount. An offer built around the main reason people hesitate, like fit or durability, sells more without cutting price.

watch.metric: conversion rate on the product page with the new offer, 14 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the offer is 10% off the first order. After: a 'free size swap' offer replaces it and conversion rises 14% with no discount cost.

jobs.job: Know the ad cost I can afford after an offer change
jobs.why: Every change to price, discount or bundle changes how much can be spent to win a sale. If ad targets are not reset, the account either overspends or holds back.

watch.metric: break-even cost per purchase at the current offer
watch.source: Shopify orders and cost per item, with Meta and Google Ads cost per purchase

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the ad target is still $30 per sale after a bundle cut profit per order to $24. After: the target resets to $22 and losing ad sets are cut.

jobs.job: Build bundles and multi-packs that raise order size without giving away margin
jobs.why: Bundles lift order size, but a deep bundle discount can make each unit less profitable than a single sale.

watch.metric: units per order and gross profit per order, 30 days
watch.source: Shopify orders and cost per item

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 12% of orders take a bundle and the 12 pack loses $2 per unit. After: 3 tiers with the middle one set as default, 30% take a bundle and every tier clears the floor.

jobs.job: Offer a guarantee that removes risk without breaking margin if claims run high
jobs.why: A strong guarantee wins buyers who are unsure. If claims run higher than planned, it costs more than it earns.

watch.metric: guarantee claims as a share of covered orders, 60 days, against plan
watch.source: Shopify refunds tagged as guarantee claims

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: no guarantee shown near the price. After: a 'wear them for 30 days' guarantee lifts conversion 9% with claims at 2%, under the 4% plan.

jobs.job: Place upsells and add-ons that add profit, not just clicks
jobs.why: An upsell with a high take rate can still lose money if it is too cheap or replaces a full-price item.

watch.metric: gross profit added per order by upsells, against a group that did not see them, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a cart add-on is taken by 18% of buyers but adds only $1.20 profit per order. After: a better item swaps in and adds $3.40.

jobs.job: Stop training buyers to wait for a sale
jobs.why: When sales come too often, buyers stop paying full price. Discounted revenue creeps up and margin falls month after month.

watch.metric: share of revenue sold at a discount, 90 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: discounted revenue rose from 35% to 58% of sales in 3 months. After: sales are cut to 2 a quarter and it falls to 40% in 2 quarters.

jobs.job: Give new and returning buyers different offers
jobs.why: Loyal buyers often come back without a discount. Giving them the same code as new buyers throws margin away.

watch.metric: discount spend per returning customer order, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 40% of returning orders use the welcome code. After: returning buyers get a free gift instead and discount spend on them falls 60%.

jobs.job: Catch sellers undercutting our price on marketplaces
jobs.why: When resellers sell below our price on Amazon or eBay, buyers stop paying our price on the site and trust drops.

watch.metric: marketplace listings below our minimum advertised price, weekly

drives.metric: site conversion rate on matched products

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 7 Amazon listings sell our 6 pack 20% under our price. After: 5 are fixed within 2 weeks after notices.

jobs.job: Plan each sale so it adds profit, not just pulls orders forward
jobs.why: A sale can steal orders from the weeks after it. The true result is profit during the sale plus the dip after, against a normal period.

watch.metric: gross profit during the sale plus the 30 days after, against the same period with no sale
watch.source: Shopify orders and cost per item

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a spring sale booked $60,000 but the next 3 weeks fell 30%. After: the model shows it lost money, and the next one is shorter and on 2 products only.

jobs.job: Use free gifts that move buyers to the order size we want
jobs.why: A gift that everyone gets costs margin and changes nothing. A gift placed on the right tier moves buyers up.

watch.metric: share of orders on the gift tier, and gift cost as a share of order value, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a free tote on every order costs 6% of order value. After: the tote moves to orders over $60 and the share of orders over $60 rises from 22% to 35%.

jobs.job: Make the pop-up signup offer pay for itself
jobs.why: A pop-up discount grows the email list, but if most signups would have bought anyway, it gives margin to the wrong people.

watch.metric: first order gross profit from pop-up signups, net of discount, 30 days
watch.source: Klaviyo signup source with Shopify orders

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 15% off for signup, and 70% of signups used it on an order they were about to place. After: a free gift offer tested against it keeps signups flat and saves $3 per order.

jobs.job: Find out if we can charge more
jobs.why: Many brands are priced from a guess made years ago. A tested price rise can add margin on every order with little loss in sales.

watch.metric: conversion rate and gross profit per visitor at the new price, 14 to 28 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the 3 pack has been $39 for 3 years while costs rose 15%. After: $42 holds conversion within 3% and gross profit per visitor rises 6%.

jobs.job: Keep the offer the same on the ad, page, cart and email
jobs.why: When the ad says 20% off and the cart shows 15%, buyers leave and some complain. One offer everywhere keeps trust.

watch.metric: checkout completion rate on ad traffic, 7 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the ad offers a free gift that the cart does not show. After: the cart shows it and checkout completion from that ad rises 11%.

jobs.job: Show prices and discounts honestly, with no made-up 'was' price
jobs.why: A 'was' price that never existed can bring legal risk and costs trust once buyers notice.

watch.metric: products showing a 'was' price with no real selling history at that price
watch.source: Shopify compare-at prices and order history

drives.metric: refund and complaint rate on sale items

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 14 products show a 'was' price never charged. After: 0, and sale pages show real past prices.

jobs.job: Clear slow stock with an offer that frees cash without cheapening the best sellers
jobs.why: Old stock ties up cash and storage. A targeted offer on those items only gets cash back without teaching buyers to wait on the core range.

watch.metric: units of stock older than 180 days sold, and cash recovered, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: $22,000 of last year's colors sit unsold. After: a 'last chance' bundle clears 60% in 30 days and frees $9,000.

jobs.job: Run referral offers that win customers for less than ads do
jobs.why: Happy buyers bring friends at a lower cost than ads, but only if the offer is worth sharing and tracked.

watch.metric: cost per referred new customer against paid new customer cost, 60 days
watch.source: Shopify orders with referral codes, and Meta and Google Ads spend

drives.metric: share of new customers from referral

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: no referral offer, paid new customers cost $38. After: a give $10 get $10 offer brings 7% of new customers at $14 each.

jobs.job: Offer pay-in-parts where it lifts sales on bigger orders
jobs.why: On bigger baskets, a split payment removes the price shock. Where it does not lift sales, the fee is wasted.

watch.metric: conversion rate on orders over $100 with pay-in-parts shown, 30 days
watch.source: Shopify orders by payment method and GA4

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: pay-in-parts is off. After: it lifts conversion on $100 plus carts by 8% and the fee is covered.

jobs.job: Use store credit instead of cash refunds where buyers accept it
jobs.why: A cash refund loses the sale. Store credit, with a small bonus, keeps the money and often brings a second order.

watch.metric: share of returns taken as store credit, 30 days

drives.metric: cash kept from returns per month

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 95% of returns are cash refunds. After: a $5 bonus on store credit moves 35% of returns to credit and keeps $6,000 a month.

jobs.job: Make 'subscribe' worth more than a flat discount, for products people reorder
jobs.why: A flat 10% off subscribe offer gives margin away and does not keep people. Perks that match how they use the product hold them longer.

watch.metric: subscribers still active at 90 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: subscribe and save 15%, and half cancel by the 3rd order. After: a free pair every 4th box keeps 65% past 90 days.
jobs.who_today: retention freelancer, only for stores that sell replenishment

jobs.job: Run offer tests one at a time so the result can be trusted
jobs.why: When 2 offer tests hit the same buyers at once, neither result means anything. Budget is spent and nothing is learned.

watch.metric: offer tests that overlap in buyers or dates
watch.source: test log in the brand brain

drives.metric: share of offer tests with a clear result

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a bundle test and a free shipping test ran on the same buyers in the same week. After: tests are staggered and each gives a clear read.

jobs.job: Refresh a tired offer in the right order before cutting price
jobs.why: When an offer stops working, the first move is often a bigger discount. Changing the ad, the words or the wrapper first keeps margin.

watch.metric: conversion rate on the refreshed offer against the old one, 14 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the welcome offer's conversion fell 20% over 6 months, and the plan is to go from 15% to 25% off. After: a new name and gift wrapper win back the lost 20% with no deeper discount.

jobs.job: Check checkout add-ons like shipping protection for profit and fairness
jobs.why: Pre-ticked add-ons can annoy buyers and break platform or state rules. Some add profit, some only add complaints.

watch.metric: add-on take rate, profit per order and complaints tagged to add-ons, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: shipping protection is pre-ticked and drives 30 tickets a month. After: it is unticked by default, keeps half the take rate, and tickets fall to 4.

jobs.job: Track gift card money owed and whether it gets used
jobs.why: Unused gift card balances are money owed to buyers. If it keeps growing, cash on the books is not really free to spend.

watch.metric: gift card balance outstanding and share redeemed, 90 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: $31,000 outstanding, up 40% in a year, and only 55% redeemed. After: a reminder email lifts redemption to 70% and brings repeat orders.
